races.name: Iglu Apprentice Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Ambishio
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby's three-year-old drops back to handicap company fresh off 11 days; hold-up style suits a slowly-run race but his form figures of 8 and 10 on Good at this trip give pause, with a peak run of 2nd on Standrd the best recent evidence — headgear (hood/p) worn again.|

runners_data.name: London Is Blue
runners_data.note: Robert Cowell's charge returns after a 79-day break, which is the key concern, but two wins on Good ground at 6f and a placed run at 5f on Good underpin strong going suitability; Jack Callan needs a prominent pitch here given there is no natural pace to chase.|

runners_data.name: Adalida
runners_data.note: Stuart Williams sends out Adalida in good recent form (win at 5f GOO, 18 days ago) with Ethan Tindall (3lb claim) in the saddle; she is a genuine hold-up type, however, and the redistribution to midfield means she may not settle where she is most effective — her STYLE_FIT of 0.92 tempers enthusiasm slightly despite that winning run.|

runners_data.name: Victor Cee
runners_data.note: Phil McEntee's gelding is the least exposed on OR=64 and has one eye-catching third at 5f on Good ground in recent history, but form figures of 5, 7, 8 dominate and headgear (visor) suggests a quirky profile; a true hold-up type displaced from his natural position, his chance here is conditional on the slow gallop that his mapping implies but cannot guarantee.|

races.paceDynamic: With all four runners carrying a hold-up profile, this 5f at Yarmouth has no natural front-runner to set the tempo, meaning the field will almost certainly drift into a pace-less sprint where whoever finds the best position from the gates and travels most smoothly will hold the advantage. Adalida and Victor Cee are the two runners redistributed from the rear — both are genuine hold-up types forced into a midfield mapping because the field is uniformly loaded with closers who cannot all settle at the back. In a race this small (four runners) with no pace-maker, the absence of early fractions typically compresses the finish and removes any significant late-run advantage. This shape most favours the horse who can switch off behind a non-existent tempo and then produce the sharpest acceleration off a slow gallop — a profile that rewards course form, recent fitness, and jockey craft over pure staying power.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Compressed Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the field crawls early and the race is decided by a short, sharp burst inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: With no pace-setter, the field will bunch and race in a tight cluster before a furious dash to the line; the first horse to pick up off the slow gallop takes the spoils.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Two Break Clear
scenarios.trigger: If one or two runners jump smartly and steal an uncontested lead by default in the absence of genuine pace.
scenarios.body: A horse that breaks well and commits to the front from the gate effectively becomes the race's only front-runner and can dictate unchallenged; a small field of hold-up types rarely organises a coordinated chase.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closer Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If one runner is held up deliberately furthest back and times a late run to catch the bunched field napping.
scenarios.body: Given the field's genuine hold-up tendencies, one horse may be anchored at the rear and produce a strong finish if the leaders tie each other up late; Adalida's recent win at this trip on Good ground makes this plausible despite her redistribution.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Springs Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If Victor Cee, having shown ability at this trip on Good ground (third, 5f, GOO), overcomes his lowest OR and finds form on the day.
scenarios.body: The lowest-weighted runner, Victor Cee has shown enough pace at 5f on similar ground to be dangerous if the pace is genuinely slow and the others fail to quicken; Connor Planas will need to position him smartly to give him any chance.

watchPoints.text: London Is Blue has been off 79 days — watch market moves at the off; if Cowell has this ready first-time-back, the absence of pace could hand Callan a soft lead by default.

Adalida's redistribution means Ethan Tindall (3lb claim) must decide early whether to anchor or push forward — if he misjudges the lack of pace and gets stuck wide, her natural finishing effort will be blunted in a race this short.
Victor Cee's visor suggests he needs to be ridden positively, but with no genuine pace he risks being left flat-footed if the sprint unfolds quickly — Connor Planas should monitor this at the stalls.

With all four runners sharing a hold-up profile, draw and early gate reactions will be unusually influential over 5f at Yarmouth — stall positions should be cross-referenced before forming final views.

races.name: Aeropak Restricted Maiden Stakes (For Horses In Bands B, C And D) (GBB Race)
4-head Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Gorgeous Mr George
runners_data.note: Dual course-and-distance winner at 8f on Good ground but steps back to 7f here; the front-running role is natural and the Yarmouth flat track suits, though his last four runs before this winning streak showed a tendency to be beaten well, so Taryn Langley (5lb claim) must manage the pace judiciously to avoid setting an overly generous target.

runners_data.name: Sea Suite
runners_data.note: Cieren Fallon is a major booking for James Owen, who is in strong form at 10/48 over 14 days; the visor is retained, the horse won at 7f Good ground last time and has a genuine hold-up profile that suits a race run at a steady-to-honest tempo — the main concern is a record showing only 1 win from 14 runs in similar going.

runners_data.name: Tryst
runners_data.note: Trained by in-form George Boughey (4/23 T14) and ridden by 3lb claimer Jack Callan, this 3yo drops back sharply from 10f to 7f, and while a 7f win exists on the record, the step down in trip combined with only 2 runs from 7 on similar going is a genuine query; the hood (headgear marked p) signals the yard expects a positive response.

runners_data.name: Izzy Fast
runners_data.note: Quick turnaround at 7 days since last run for Philip McBride's charge; this horse's natural inclination is to race up with or near the pace, but with a congested prominent group ahead, it is likely to find itself further back than ideal — its best recent form has come at 6f and 7f on Good ground, so the distance is fine, but the positional compromise is real.

runners_data.name: Up The Agenda
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy's booking elevates this horse's appeal significantly; Jack Morland is 2/7 over 14 days and the horse has won twice at 6f on Soft and Standard, stepping up to 7f on Good for the first time — the trip extension and going switch are both unknowns, and its prominent style should allow Murphy to travel comfortably just off Gorgeous Mr George.

runners_data.name: Dion Baker
runners_data.note: Exceptional recent form — 5 wins from last 5 runs including four consecutive 7f Good ground victories — and Michael Wigham is 2/8 in the last 14 days; the horse's natural game is to race prominently or even lead, and being pushed back by the race shape against horses like Gorgeous Mr George and Up The Agenda stealing the rail is the key risk that tempers its theoretical claims.

races.paceDynamic: Gorgeous Mr George is the confirmed front-runner here and should lead from the outset, with Up The Agenda and Dion Baker likely to press into prominent positions behind — though with multiple horses wanting to race prominently, some jostling for early position is probable before a rhythm is established. Gorgeous Mr George has won twice at 8f on Good ground recently and steps back to 7f, a trip where his finishing effort over the final furlong will determine whether he can hold on or get swallowed late. The field holds more prominent-running types than the shape can accommodate: Dion Baker and Izzy Fast are genuine front-runners or prominent racers in truth, but with Gorgeous Mr George setting the terms and Up The Agenda alongside, both are likely to be shuffled further back than they'd ideally want. This race shape — a single horse dictating at a sustainable tempo over 7f on a flat Yarmouth track — strongly favours horses that can sit just off the pace and produce a measured late challenge, with Sea Suite and Tryst the primary hold-up beneficiaries if the pace is honest but not punishing.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Gorgeous Mr George secures an uncontested lead and dials down the tempo to a sustainable gallop.
scenarios.body: Gorgeous Mr George dictates from the front unchallenged, setting fractions that keep energy in reserve for the final furlong on this flat track; the lack of genuine pressure means he reaches the final 2f with horses behind unable to fully wind up their challenges. Prominent racers just off the pace benefit most, with Up The Agenda ideally placed to pounce if the lead weakens late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Runners Swoop Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace proves honest enough to stretch the front runners and leave them vulnerable in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: Sea Suite and Tryst, operating from hold-up positions, collect a tiring leader inside the final furlong as the pace takes its toll on Gorgeous Mr George; Yarmouth's flat, straight 7f tests stamina only modestly, so the pace must genuinely be brisk for this to materialise. Sea Suite's visor and Cieren Fallon's big-race pedigree are assets in this shape, while Tryst's step back to 7f from 10f starts requires some caution.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Types Emerge
scenarios.trigger: If early positional battles disrupt both the leaders and the hold-up horses, leaving a clean run through the field as the decisive factor.
scenarios.body: Dion Baker and Izzy Fast, though mapped to midfield against their natural inclinations, could capitalise if the race fragments around them — Dion Baker in particular has exceptional recent form with five wins from his last five at this distance and course type. However, both carry the weight of being out of their preferred role, and the probability of this scenario delivering is structurally limited by that redistribution.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Carnage
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely fierce and multiple prominent types burn each other out completely.
scenarios.body: A fast early duel between Gorgeous Mr George and Up The Agenda could detonate the race, leaving the entire field to sprint for a prize among tiring horses in the final furlong; Sea Suite with headgear (visor) and a strong trainer in form (James Owen T14: 10/48) represents the best-placed horse to benefit from wholesale front-runner capitulation. This is the least likely shape on current pace evidence but cannot be entirely dismissed given the compressed field.

watchPoints.text: Gorgeous Mr George sets the pace unchallenged — if Taryn Langley (5lb claim) is unable to judge the fractions correctly over 7f and goes too fast, the entire race shape inverts in the final furlong.

Dion Baker's outstanding recent form (five wins) is in direct tension with a race shape that will push it out of its preferred prominent position — watch for early traffic as Darragh Keenan attempts to reclaim ground.

Up The Agenda has Oisin Murphy booked and a trainer in form, but the 7f trip on Good turf is an unexplored combination for this horse — watch market moves as a guide to stable confidence on the trip extension.

Sea Suite's visor is retained and Cieren Fallon is a booking that consistently outperforms trainer strike rates — if the pace is genuinely honest, this horse has the profile to arrive late with authority.

Izzy Fast ran just 7 days ago and its true running style is hold-up/prominent; monitor how Hector Crouch positions the horse in the opening furlong as any scramble for prominent slots will define whether it has any chance of running to its best.

races.name: Doublebase Classified Stakes

runners_data.name: Duke Orsino
runners_data.note: A deep hold-up performer for Jenkins who has never won in 14 career starts and whose recent form string of -90445 includes two STA wins/places that may flatter; 20 days between runs is fine, but without a finish to rival in a dawdle-then-sprint this horse's lack of a win under any conditions is damning.

runners_data.name: Highland Harvey
runners_data.note: Arnolda's charge has placed twice at 12f on Good ground which is directly relevant here, but is explicitly tagged as fading in the finish — a significant concern in a race that will almost certainly become a pure sprint — and its hold-up style means it will be towards the rear of whatever sprint develops.

runners_data.name: Spaceage Love Song
runners_data.note: Bell and Murphy is a compelling combination and Murphy's ability to read a race and find clear running is the biggest tactical asset in this field; won at 12f on STA last time out and has a 2nd at 10f on Good, making this trip and going plausible, though a wind op (hg:v) is flagged and a return to form at 1m3½f is needed.

runners_data.name: Suitcase Smith
runners_data.note: Egan takes over for Berry on a horse whose six-run form in similar going (6/8, 0W0P) reflects persistent mediocrity; the form string of 6-0796 on Good and Soft includes no placing closer than sixth, and there is nothing in the record to suggest this horse finds the sprint finish that this race shape will demand.

runners_data.name: Ten Ten Twenty
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old who has won at 14f on this surface type and placed three times at 12-14f, giving the strongest staying profile in the field — if the race is even marginally honest in its fractions, Fallon on Jeffreys' veteran is best equipped to grind out the stamina argument; 74 days off is the only concern.

runners_data.name: Cormorant Rock
runners_data.note: Boyle's three-year-old carries a 3lb allowance which is meaningful in a close-rated field, and three of four runs have been on Good ground; a natural hold-up type whose best result is a 4th at 8f on Good, so the step up to 1m3½f is the obvious question, but Heard has ridden well for Boyle recently.

runners_data.name: Fletcher
runners_data.note: Cosgrave takes the ride for Boyle on a three-year-old who shares the 3lb allowance with stablemate Cormorant Rock, but whose form of 0-4767 across five runs on Good and Soft shows no wins and placings only in modest company; finishing positions have hovered consistently in the 6th-7th range on Good, offering limited confidence in a race that demands a decisive finish.

races.paceDynamic: With every single runner in this seven-horse field carrying a hold-up profile, there is no confirmed front-runner and no horse with any meaningful history of setting the pace — meaning the race will almost certainly crawl into a dawdle before erupting into a sprint finish over the final two furlongs of this 1m3½f trip at Yarmouth. The field will bunch up early, runners jostling for handy positions without anyone truly committed to leading, and the race will compress into a cavalry charge off the home turn. Because all seven runners are genuine hold-up types — Duke Orsino, Highland Harvey, Spaceage Love Song, Suitcase Smith, Ten Ten Twenty, Cormorant Rock, and Fletcher — the map is forced to redistribute five of them to midfield simply to fill the race shape, but in reality none of these horses has any natural inclination to lead or press from the front. The tactical verdict is clear: whoever can position most cleverly in the pack, travel smoothly through the slow early fractions, and produce the strongest sustained finish in the final two furlongs will dominate — this race shape overwhelmingly favours the horse with the best pure turn-of-foot and whose jockey secures the clearest run in a compressed, sprint-style finish.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Blanket Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the race drifts along at a crawl before detonating in a two-furlong dash, with the entire field arriving together at the turn.
scenarios.body: The race compresses into a single mass and separates purely on finishing speed and racing luck in traffic; the winner is whichever runner produces the sharpest, cleanest surge from the pack.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Stamina Edges Out Speed
scenarios.trigger: If a fractionally stronger early gallop stretches the field and the closing stages become a test of staying power rather than pure sprint.
scenarios.body: A slightly more honest early clip means the field is less tightly grouped off the turn, rewarding the horse that stays on most relentlessly to the line; the sprint-finish specialists get found out late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Positional Advantage Wins
scenarios.trigger: If one runner — most likely Spaceage Love Song or Cormorant Rock — settles in the ideal spot just off the non-existent pace and travels into the race without being crowded.
scenarios.body: A clean passage from a handy position allows that runner to dictate its own race and punch clear before the pack fully organises, making jockeyship from Murphy or Heard critical.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Traffic Carnage Unpicks Field
scenarios.trigger: If the sprint-finish chaos produces significant interference, with several runners blocked and only those widest or best-placed emerging late.
scenarios.body: In a bottleneck finish on a sharp Yarmouth straight, horses with wider positions or those whose jockeys anticipate the trouble earliest benefit disproportionately; Oisin Murphy on Spaceage Love Song or Cieren Fallon on Ten Ten Twenty most likely to navigate cleanly.

watchPoints.text: With no pace in the race at all, watch for the opening quarter-mile to be absurdly slow — any runner that fails to travel smoothly through the early crawl and then gets caught flat-footed when the sprint ignites is immediately at a disadvantage, and this could expose horses like Suitcase Smith and Duke Orsino who have no form in fast-finish races.

Oisin Murphy on Spaceage Love Song is the most significant jockey upgrade in the race — watch how Murphy positions the horse in the first three furlongs, as his ability to secure clean air in a seven-horse sprint finish could be the decisive tactical factor.

Ten Ten Twenty is 74 days off the track and wears a tongue-tie for the first time (hg:tp) — watch in the parade ring and early in the race for any signs of ring-rustiness or a horse that hasn't trained through to peak fitness after a 10-week absence.

Highland Harvey is explicitly flagged as fading in the finish and sits second-highest in market expectation based on recent form — watch whether Ray Dawson attempts to compensate by taking a more prominent early position, which would be entirely against the horse's natural pattern and could backfire.

Cormorant Rock and Fletcher are both Jim Boyle-trained three-year-olds with the same jockey-trainer connections, same weight allowance, and similar hold-up profiles — watch whether Boyle has a clear first and second string or whether these two could interfere with each other's tactical plans in the sprint finish.

races.name: Bazuka Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Dark Side Thunder
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse with consistent 6f good-ground form (two placed efforts in this exact combination), wears a visor, 25 days since last run, and trainer Jessica Macey has a flat recent record of 0/3 over 14 days — will need the race to set up late.|

runners_data.name: Startled Lady
runners_data.note: Three-year-old filly ridden by Neil Callan for William Knight (3/19 in 14 days, solid yard form), holds a course-relevant placed effort over 6f on good, but most recent runs have been over 7f on softer — dropping back in trip on better ground is the key question.|

runners_data.name: Viking Glory
runners_data.note: Cieren Fallon takes the ride for James Owen (10/48 in 14 days), and while this horse's card marks it as hold-up, its true natural inclination is rearward — it is shown in midfield only because the field is saturated with closers, and it may find itself unable to settle where it wants; handles good, wears a tongue tie, no wins in seven turf starts.|

runners_data.name: Lieutenant Sir
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy partners this Archie Watson-trained gelding, whose sole win came over 6f on good at this course — the course and conditions tick the boxes — but it is a genuine closer shuffled toward midfield because there is no room at the rear, tempering the significance of that form angle.|

runners_data.name: Komodo Rose
runners_data.note: Has placed over 7f in similar conditions but has not run over 6f and most form is on softer; a natural hold-up type whose race position will be dictated by the field rather than preference, making her effective running style unpredictable on the day; Ray Dawson rides, wore a hood.|

runners_data.name: Superstorm
runners_data.note: Charlie Fellowes's three-year-old is in good form (3/12 trainer strike rate over 14 days), placed twice in recent starts including a second over 7f on standard, but the step up to a genuine sprint on good ground tests whether the speed is sharp enough — a true closer racing into an unfamiliar midfield berth.|

races.paceDynamic: With all six runners classified as hold-up types, this 6f Yarmouth handicap has no confirmed front runner, meaning the early gallop is likely to be modest and the field will bunch together before a sprint develops in the final two furlongs. Dark Side Thunder and Startled Lady are the two runners whose natural style places them genuinely at the rear, while Viking Glory, Lieutenant Sir, Komodo Rose, and Superstorm are all true hold-up horses redistributed into midfield on the map because this field contains more closers than the shape can accommodate at the back. The four redistributed runners — Viking Glory, Lieutenant Sir, Komodo Rose, and Superstorm — are unlikely to secure their natural rearward berth and will be shuffled forward out of role, potentially creating a moderate mid-race tempo before a compressed sprint finish. Given the absence of pace and the likelihood of a slow-run, late-burst contest, horses with a sharp turn of foot over 6f on good turf — particularly those with form in similar conditions — are best placed, while pure hold-up specialists who need a true run to generate momentum face the most risk in a race where the race may not be truly run.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sprint Finish Suits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop is slow and the field concertinas, producing a two-furlong dash from the two-pole.
scenarios.body: With minimal early pace, the race becomes a test of raw speed and finishing kick over the final quarter-mile, compressing the entire field into a single wave.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Redistributed Types Force Tempo
scenarios.trigger: If the displaced hold-up horses push forward and inadvertently inject pace into the middle stages.
scenarios.body: A more honest gallop develops as Viking Glory, Lieutenant Sir, or Superstorm find themselves unable to settle at the rear and press forward, stretching the field.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Swamped By Pace
scenarios.trigger: If one or two runners push forward aggressively early and set a genuinely strong pace for 6f.
scenarios.body: Those horses forced wide or back struggle to pick up, while any runner who tracked a good position in the first half of the race inherits the advantage.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Left Flat Footed
scenarios.trigger: If the race is run at a crawl before a sudden sharp acceleration that catches the true hold-up types cold.
scenarios.body: Dark Side Thunder and Startled Lady, anchored at the back by genuine preference, find the winning move has gone before they can launch their run.

watchPoints.text: Viking Glory, Lieutenant Sir, Komodo Rose, and Superstorm are all genuine closers forced into midfield — if any of these drift back to their natural position the field could be dangerously compressed in the straight with nowhere to go.

Lieutenant Sir's sole course-and-distance win is a powerful flag, but Oisin Murphy will need to manage the horse's position carefully given it cannot settle as far back as it prefers in this field shape.

Dark Side Thunder's going record on turf stands at 0 wins from 4 placed efforts in similar conditions — the horse shows up without converting, which may indicate a positional handicap in a slow-run race where front rank matters most.

Startled Lady drops from 7f to 6f on better ground than her recent starts — if the tempo is slow and the race is a sprint, the drop in trip may actually sharpen her finishing effort rather than disadvantage her.

With going listed as unknown at Yarmouth, any last-minute ground report should be monitored — several runners in this field carry headgear or have specific going preferences that could shift the shape materially.
